first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the concurrent declines in onboarding completion and activation, with prior evidence of improved time-to-value and early adoption. Promotional pricing could counter the competitor but has documented 30-day retention harm, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Verify the most relevant onboarding evidence and the key downstream risk of the strongest alternative.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified source directly addresses both current declines: shortening onboarding increased completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention by 3%. Promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure because its qualified-revenue lift came with a verified 12% retention decline and failure at first renewal, conflicting with the sustainable long-term qualified-revenue objective. A controlled experiment preserves uncertainty about whether the historical effect will replicate under current conditions.
